scope: Independent arithmetic and convention audit; not economic endorsement. The producer valuation script was not imported or executed.
method: 45-digit Decimal reconstruction from frozen product, corporate, Foundry, transition, tax and treasury inputs. Post2030 product revenue rebuilt from unit, ASP and category-growth drivers. DCF tails summed through3000 instead of the producer Gordon formula.
findings: Operating tax is recomputed before ordinary debt effects; SBC remains economically charged.
Minority reserves and all-in lease cash are deducted once, without duplicate NCI or associated lease liability subtraction.
Capitalized interest is removed from physical capex and retained once in treasury. The separate next-year eight-year tax recovery is included once per valuation date.
Historical financing benefits reside in endpoint cash; only future benefits enter endpoint PV. Fixed nominal debt supports a flat nominal benefit tail.
Capital-credit collections and basis-loss charges are dated and finite; no duplicate receivable asset is added.
Working capital is included once in capital productivity, and terminal growth is funded.
Escrow cash is paired with full pending shares. Classiq is charged at its dates, with no second charge after its payments enter cash.
limitations: End2026 reference is not November3 fair value.
Economic cash after cash-equivalent SBC and minority reserves is not bank cash or an intrayear liquidity test.
Tax rates, credit eligibility, capitalization recovery and D&A are normalizations, not statutory schedules.
Claims, private assets, debt carrying values and supplier-capacity allowance remain approximations.
Operating recovery, terminal margins and capital productivity are prospective judgments. Passing arithmetic does not validate them or establish an attractive short.
audit_iteration_note: An initial direct tail ending2300 left about5e-7B truncation error in the11% control. Extending the independent tail to3000 removed this numerical truncation; producer inputs and output were unchanged.
